audit.whatIsWrong: Titan's Wrath is absent from every string in both layers. His only defensive cooldown, and the thing that turns his autos into AoE damage over time, is not mentioned once.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Nautilus gains a temporary Shield. While it persists, his Attacks deal damage over time to his target and surrounding enemies.' It is a flat 12 seconds at every rank. Against a burst pattern that shield is the difference between a trade won and a trade wasted, and the entry told the player to look for windows without naming the one cooldown that decides whether the window is real.
audit.corrected: Named with its flat 12s in spikes[0].text, mid, whys[2], breakdown.cooldowns and wants.foe[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: 'The armor-pen passive makes that combo actually land' appears in spikes[1].text, wants.you[1], mid and whys[4]. Public Execution has no passive and no penetration.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Ambessa blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line of her choosing and suppresses them upon her arrival. She then slams the enemy into the ground where they take damage and are stunned.' What makes the level-6 all-in work is the suppression — a suppressed Nautilus cannot hook, cannot Riptide and cannot cast Depth Charge. That is a much stronger and entirely true reason.
audit.corrected: All four now say the suppression shuts his chain off, and the itemisation call for penetration stands on its own in wants.you[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: 'His next ~15 seconds have no way to reach you' is the closest thing to a number in the entry, and it is an approximation of the wrong figure.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10 — 14 at rank 1, dropping to 10. The other numbers the entry needs and does not have: Riptide 7/6.5/6/5.5/5, Titan's Wrath a flat 12, Depth Charge 120/100/80 against Public Execution's 130/115/100. His ultimate coming back ten seconds sooner than hers is the honest reason level 6 is only a window and not a takeover.
audit.corrected: Real numbers in spikes[2].text, mid, whys[3], whys[5], breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dredge Line is described only as a hook that pulls you in.
audit.why: Riot's text has a second clause: 'Colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus towards it.' A whiffed hook is not automatically a free window if there is a wall behind him — he can still reposition with it. In a top lane full of terrain that changes how much a sidestep actually buys you, and it is the difference between 'he has no way to move' and 'he has no way to reach you'.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text now says he cannot reach YOU, and early notes the wall pull.

audit.whatIsWrong: late ends on 'Anti-heal does nothing into a champion with no sustain' — a sentence about something that does not apply.
audit.why: A line whose content is the absence of an interaction is filler, and the space is better spent on what does apply: Titan's Wrath is a shield rather than a heal, so the counter is forcing it out on its flat 12 seconds rather than buying Grievous Wounds.
audit.corrected: Replaced that clause in late with the Titan's Wrath timing.

edits.before: His Dredge Line hook into a Staggering Blow root on the follow-up auto is the whole problem early — every time he lands it he pins you out of your Drakehound dash-weave and chains Riptide on top, and your Q and E cooldowns are far too long at levels 1-3 to trade back through that lockdown. Don't sit in hook range to last-hit; farm from max distance with the tip of your Cunning Sweep cone. If he whiffs Dredge Line, that's your only real window — dash in, land Sundering Slam plus an empowered auto, and peel off before his root comes back up.
edits.after: His Dredge Line hook into a Staggering Blow root on the follow-up auto is the whole problem early — every time he lands it he pins you out of your Drakehound dash-weave and chains Riptide on top, and your Q and E cooldowns are far too long at levels 1-3 to trade back through that. Don't sit in hook range to last-hit; farm from distance with the blades of your Cunning Sweep cone. If he whiffs the hook you get 14s at rank 1 — dash in, land Sundering Slam and an empowered auto, and peel off before the root resets.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still his — your cooldowns are at their longest and his hook-root-slow chain out-trades your dash pattern, so concede the wave and farm toward 6. At 6 the lane flips for one window: Public Execution blinks you behind him, suppresses him out of his CC chain, and the armor-pen passive plus the crash-down stun lets your Q-auto-Q burst actually connect — all-in here when his Q hook is down and his jungler isn't pathing top. That R is your equalizer against a target who otherwise just chains CC and walks away tankier than you.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still his — your cooldowns are at their longest and his hook-root-slow chain out-trades your dash pattern, so concede the wave and farm toward 6. At 6 the lane flips for one window: Public Execution blinks 1250 to the farthest champion in the line and suppresses him, and a suppressed Nautilus cannot hook, cannot Riptide and cannot start Depth Charge. All-in with his Q on its 14s and Titan's Wrath already spent. Note his R is 120s against your 130s — the window is yours only once.

edits.before: This is where he takes the lane back. He's a tank stacking armor and Plated Steelcaps, your damage is entirely physical, so the Q-auto-Q combo that halves a squishy just bounces off him — meanwhile his hook, passive root, Riptide slow and Depth Charge knockup form a full peel chain that pins you for his team. Don't try to solo-kill a two-item Nautilus; use Public Execution to blink past him onto his carries and let your team handle the front line. Anti-heal does nothing into a champion with no sustain — early armor pen and ending the game before he's a three-item wall is the only real answer.
edits.after: This is where he takes the lane back. He's a tank stacking armor and Plated Steelcaps, your damage is entirely physical, so the Q-auto-Q combo that halves a squishy just bounces off him — meanwhile his hook, passive root, Riptide slow and Depth Charge knockup form a full peel chain that pins you for his team. Don't try to solo-kill a two-item Nautilus; use Public Execution to blink past him onto his carries. Titan's Wrath is a shield, not a heal, so force it out on its flat 12s rather than buying anti-heal, and end the game before he is a three-item wall.

notes: The biggest gap was an absence rather than an error: Titan's Wrath, a flat 12-second shield that also turns his autos into AoE damage over time, was not mentioned anywhere in either layer, so every 'find your window' instruction was missing the cooldown that decides whether the window exists. The recurring 'armor-pen passive' on Public Execution was removed again — the suppression is the real reason the level-6 all-in works, and it is stronger: a suppressed Nautilus cannot cast any of his three CC abilities. Two smaller precisions: Dredge Line also pulls him toward terrain, so a sidestep denies him YOU rather than denying him movement; and his Depth Charge at 120s comes back ten seconds sooner than her 130s Public Execution, which is why level 6 reads as Skill rather than Ambessa on the chart. Sides and ratings left untouched; there is no nautilus/ambessa mirror yet.
